newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan confirms U.S. firm's giant mall project.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan confirms U.S. firm's giant mall project.

text.p: Taipei on Friday confirmed that an unidentified U.S. firm planned to build a multibillion-dollar shopping mall complex on reclaimed land in southern Taiwan, but said the project was still in the early planning stages.
State television quoted Economic Minister Wang Chih-kang as saying the plan was "not yet mature", but that his ministry would help to see the giant project realised.
"The Economic Ministry will have a special task force to help the firm with its project in the future," Wang said.
He gave no further details, the broadcast said.
Taiwan's United Daily News said the U.S. firm planned to invest T$100 billion (US$3.6 billion) to build a commercial complex on reclaimed land near the southern port of Kaohsiung.
Once realised, it would be the biggest foreign investment in Taiwan ever, the mass-circulation paper said.
The United Daily News quoted an unnamed economics ministry official as saying the U.S. firm has contacted the ministry but demanded confidentiality before formally seeking approval.
A spokeswoman in the ministry's public affairs department said she knew nothing of the reported project and declined to comment further.

Taipei is striving to develop the island as an Asia-Pacific operations hub for multinational firms and envisages Kaohsiung, one of the world's top container ports, becoming a regional transshipment centre.
